metrics.description: Whether the report correctly identifies the design as clean (true negative rate on this clean-design case); scored 1.0 if infected=false and suspect_nodes empty, else 0.0.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of benign rare-activity nets (reset tree, init counter, saturation comparator) incorrectly listed in suspect_nodes; must be 0 for a passing submission.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Wall-clock time taken by evaluate.py to parse and grade the submitted trojan_report.json (and optional toolchain cross-check), reported in seconds.
metrics.name: inference_latency

acceptance_criteria: submission/trojan_report.json parses as valid JSON matching the pinned schema.
rationale references at least one real net/module name from gate_netlist.v and explains why rare nets are benign, not a generic unsupported assertion.
A naive baseline submission that flags rare nets as trojans (infected=true with non-empty suspect_nodes) must FAIL evaluation.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: gate_netlist.v is a clean, Trojan-free synthesized netlist. It contains legitimate low-activity/rare-triggering logic (an active-low async reset tree, a one-time power-on initialization counter, and a rarely-taken saturation/overflow branch in the datapath) that superficially resembles trojan trigger circuitry (high fan-in AND of many control signals feeding a rarely-active net) but is fully justified by the design's documented functional intent in design_brief.md and is exercised/reachable under normal documented operation. The correct report is infected=false with suspect_nodes=[].

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Parse submission/trojan_report.json and check infected==false exactly; any true verdict fails this requirement regardless of listed suspect_nodes.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly classify the design as NOT infected (infected=false) despite the presence of low-toggle-probability nets such as the async reset tree, power-on init counter, and saturation branch.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check suspect_nodes array is empty (len==0). A non-empty list, even if it names only benign nets, fails this requirement since it demonstrates over-flagging of rare-but-legitimate logic.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must not flag any of the benign rare-activity nets (the reset synchronizer chain, init_counter logic, or overflow/saturation comparator output) as suspect nodes, i.e. suspect_nodes must be empty.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check the rationale text is non-generic (references specific net/module names from the netlist, e.g. the reset tree or init counter) and does not itself claim suspicious behavior; substantive grading is done by a grader comparing rationale content against the hidden design brief's documented rare paths.
security_requirements.requirement: The rationale must demonstrate the analyst distinguished rare-but-functionally-justified logic from actual trojan trigger/payload structures, rather than making an unjustified blanket claim.

hidden_spec.threat_model: A naive or overly aggressive rare-net detector flags any net with low toggle probability as a suspected trojan trigger, without checking whether that rare activity is functionally justified (e.g. reset, power-on init, saturation/overflow handling documented in the design brief). This produces false positives that waste analyst time, cause legitimate designs to be scrapped or re-spun, and erode trust in the detection tool, eventually causing analysts to ignore real alerts (alert fatigue).

constraints: Do not modify any file under inputs/; only create/modify submission/trojan_report.json.
The netlist and design brief are self-contained; no external IP or datasheets are required to complete the analysis.
Optional cross-checks may use yosys/iverilog/vvp on inputs/gate_netlist.v but are not required to produce the report.
expected_outputs: submission/trojan_report.json containing an infected boolean verdict
a suspect_nodes array listing any net/gate names implicated as trigger or payload logic (empty if the design is judged clean)
a short rationale string describing the structural/functional evidence used to reach the verdict

functional_requirements.requirement: submission/trojan_report.json must be valid JSON with exactly these top-level fields: 'infected' (boolean), 'suspect_nodes' (array of strings, net or gate instance names exactly as they appear in gate_netlist.v), 'rationale' (non-empty string), and 'confidence' (number between 0 and 1).
Every name listed in 'suspect_nodes' must correspond to an actual wire or gate instance identifier that appears verbatim in inputs/gate_netlist.v.
If 'infected' is true, 'suspect_nodes' must contain at least one entry; if 'infected' is false, 'suspect_nodes' must be an empty array.
The 'rationale' field must reference at least one specific net or module name found in gate_netlist.v (not a generic statement), demonstrating the analysis actually inspected the provided netlist.

public_spec.interface: Submission file: submission/trojan_report.json. Required JSON schema: {"infected": boolean, "suspect_nodes": string[], "rationale": string, "confidence": number in [0,1]}. Each string in suspect_nodes must exactly match a wire/net/instance identifier token present in inputs/gate_netlist.v. The evaluator (evaluate.py) reads inputs/gate_netlist.v, inputs/design_brief.md, and inputs/primary_io.txt for reference and grades only submission/trojan_report.json against hidden ground truth; it may optionally invoke yosys/iverilog/vvp on the netlist to cross-check claims but the verdict is scored from the submitted JSON.
public_spec.objective: You are given a small gate-level netlist (post-synthesis style, structural Verilog) for a control/datapath module. Analyze the netlist and produce a trojan analysis report that states whether the design is infected with a hardware Trojan and, if so, lists the suspect nodes (nets/gates) that form the trigger and payload logic. Your analysis should be based on structural and functional inspection of the netlist: fan-in/fan-out patterns, rare-condition trigger logic, unused or dead logic paths, and comparison against the stated functional intent in the design brief.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json with fields: infected (bool), suspect_nodes (array of strings), rationale (string), confidence (number 0-1). No other files should be modified.
